title: The Impact of Using a Non-motorised Physical Assistance Device on the Prevention of Musculoskeletal Disorders Amongst Care-givers
official: The Impact of Using a Non-motorised Physical Assistance Device on the Prevention of Musculoskeletal Disorders Amongst Care-givers
summary: This experimental study uses a Single-Case Experimental Design (SCED) with multiple baselines across participants to evaluate the impact of a non motorized assistive device (DAP) on muscle effort in care givers during their professional activities. Each participant completes a 12-day protocol consisting of three phases (A1 - B - A2), with the initial baseline (A1, no device) randomized between 2 and 6 days, followed by a 6-day intervention phase (B, wearing the non-motorized DAP), and a final withdrawal phase (A2, no device) adjusted to complete the 12-day period. Muscle effort is continuously quantified as a percentage of maximum voluntary contraction using mechanomyographic sensors (MOTEN Technologies) placed on the lumbar and biceps muscles, as well as the quadriceps at the Fondation Saint-Hélier site.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 years and older.
* Height between 160 cm and 200 cm.
* Professional care-giver working in SMR (Medical and Rehabilitation Care) or medico-social departments of partner healthcare facilities.
* Willing to wear the non-motorized DAP under the conditions defined by the protocol.
* Affiliated with or beneficiary of a national social security scheme.
* Having provided free and informed written consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Self-reported back, leg, or knee pathology that raises doubts regarding the safe use of the non-motorized DAP without prior medical clearance.
* Pregnant, parturient, or breastfeeding women.
* Persons deprived of liberty by a judicial or administrative decision (including legal guardianship, trusteeship, or court protection).
* Persons receiving psychiatric care or admitted to a healthcare or social establishment for reasons other than research.
* Persons in emergency situations unable to express prior informed consent.
